items.title: Inference with AI-Generated Covariates
items.desc: Duan and Pelger show that treating LLM-extracted features (sentiment scores, classifications, expectations) as observed covariates can invalidate downstream inference when hallucination and look-ahead bias produce systematic, input-dependent errors, and they propose corrections. [NBER WP 35481, issued week of 2026-07-20]

items.title: Training AI for When Humans Will Use It
items.desc: Bryan and Gans argue the economic value of an AI depends on the decision environment it is embedded in — how humans verify, query and combine its predictions — and model how training should be targeted to that downstream use. [NBER WP 35490, issued week of 2026-07-20]

items.title: Vector Search As Nearest Neighbor Matching: RAG-based Policy Learning in Causal Inference
items.desc: Proposes one- and two-step policy-learning methods built on retrieval-augmented generation, formalizing RAG-based action selection in the potential-outcome framework with vector search acting as nearest-neighbor matching in embedding space. [arXiv econ.EM, posted 2026-07-20]

items.title: Econometrics with Pre-Trained Embeddings for Unstructured Data
items.desc: Develops econometric theory for using off-the-shelf pre-trained embeddings of images and text as inputs to empirical economic analysis, avoiding the cost of training bespoke machine-learning models on unstructured data. [arXiv econ.EM, posted 2026-07-19]

items.title: Rationalizing Boltzmann Rationality: An Axiomatic Characterization of Entropy-Regularized Policies
items.desc: Gives a decision-theoretic axiomatization of the softmax/entropy-regularized policy that is the default model of stochastic choice in reinforcement learning, resolving the tension between the entropy bonus and standard choice axioms. [arXiv cs.LG + econ.TH, posted 2026-07-19]

items.title: Bank Runs With and Without Bank Failure
items.desc: Correia, Luck and Verner apply large language models to historical newspapers to build a database of 3,984 runs on individual U.S. banks from 1863 to 1934, then use it to study what causes runs and when they end in failure. [NBER WP 35504, issued week of 2026-07-20]

items.title: Volatility Disagreement in the Options Market
items.desc: Bali, Kelly and Mörke construct a stock-level disagreement measure from the cross-sectional dispersion of realized-variance forecasts produced by heterogeneous machine-learning models, and show it predicts returns on delta-hedged straddles. [NBER WP 35500, issued week of 2026-07-20]

items.title: AlphaZeroBeta: Deep Reinforcement Learning for Market-Neutral Portfolios
items.desc: A deep RL framework pairing a CNN-GRU policy trained with Recurrent PPO and a reward balancing excess return, benchmark correlation and transaction costs; 2014-2024 backtests across seven equity indices beat baselines on Sharpe while staying near beta-zero. [arXiv q-fin.PM, posted 2026-07-20]

items.title: Abliteration Is Not a Scalpel: Off-Target Effects of Refusal Removal on Decision Disposition Across Model Families
items.desc: Using 21,600 weekly up/down calls on Warsaw Stock Exchange equities as a probe, the paper shows that removing an LLM's refusal direction makes models systematically more optimistic and less hedged — a materially different decision-maker when deployed as a trading agent. [arXiv cs.LG + q-fin.CP, posted 2026-07-19]

sections.name: 📦 Operations & Supply Chain (INFORMS: Management Science, M&SOM, Operations Research)

items.title: The biggest winners of the American economy fear they're sinking fast
items.desc: Repeated layoffs and pressure to automate roles have left tech workers anxious even as their employers post record profits; economists quoted expect the same squeeze to reach other white-collar occupations. [Washington Post, 2026-07-19]

items.title: American A.I. Giants Face Fresh Tests
items.desc: DealBook's rundown of the pressures converging on the largest U.S. AI companies, including competition from China and the market's expectations heading into Alphabet's results. [NYT DealBook, 2026-07-20]

items.title: Why Silicon Valley Can't Stop Looking Over Its Shoulder at China
items.desc: How Chinese model releases and cheaper compute are reshaping the competitive and investment calculus for American AI firms. [NYT, 2026-07-20]

items.title: Google Is Building an A.I. Fence Around the Internet It Once Championed
items.desc: As AI answers replace links, Google is enclosing content it once helped distribute — with consequences for publisher revenue and the economics of the open web. [NYT, 2026-07-20]

items.title: 'Vibecoded' Apps Are Flooding the App Store. Is That Good for Apple?
items.desc: AI coding tools have sharply lowered the cost of shipping an app, raising questions about quality, discovery and the economics of Apple's marketplace. [NYT, 2026-07-20]

items.title: Step Into the 'Zone of Genius' (Before A.I. Takes Your Job)
items.desc: A look at how career advice and the market for white-collar skills are being reframed around what automation cannot yet do. [NYT Business, 2026-07-19]
